examples.en: He cleverly hid his lie.
Ads cleverly play on people's feelings.
The culprit slyly kept avoiding the police.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 질문을 교묘히 돌려서 대답했어요.
examples.en: That person skillfully dodged the question when answering.
Some people cleverly take advantage of the rules.

examples.ko: 중요한 조건이 작은 글씨로 교묘히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The important condition was slyly written in small print.

explain: '교묘하다'의 부사형으로, 솜씨가 좋다는 뜻도 있지만 속이거나 피하는 장면에서 꾀 있게 한다는 느낌으로 자주 어울려요. 단순히 똑똑하게 한 일에는 '영리하게', '능숙하게'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '교묘하다'. It can mean skillfully, but it often fits scenes of deceiving or evading with a sense of cunning. For something simply done smartly, '영리하게' or '능숙하게' is more natural.

examples.ko: 한 번 이겼다고 기고만장해서 연습도 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so full of himself after one win that he doesn't even practice.
My younger sibling got cocky after being praised.
If you get too cocky, it's easy to make mistakes.
He boasted with a cocky look on his face.
The newcomer acted cocky and got scolded.
Don't get cocky just because your grades went up.

explain: 주로 '기고만장하다' 꼴로 써서, 잘나가거나 칭찬을 받고 우쭐해서 거만하게 구는 모습을 말해요. 좋은 뜻이 아니라 흉보거나 주의를 줄 때 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '우쭐하다', '으스대다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '기고만장하다', describing someone acting arrogant and cocky after succeeding or being praised. It is negative, used for criticizing or warning, and similar words include '우쭐하다' and '으스대다'.

en: arbitrary; dogmatic; acting on one's own judgment or beliefs

examples.ko: 팀장님이 독단적으로 일정을 바꿔서 다들 당황했어요.
examples.en: The team leader changed the schedule on his own, and everyone was flustered.

examples.ko: 독단적인 결정은 나중에 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A unilateral decision can become a problem later.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 성격이 독단적이라 의견을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: He is so dogmatic that he hardly listens to opinions.

examples.ko: 왜 저한테 안 물어보고 독단적으로 정했어요?
examples.en: Why did you decide on your own without asking me?
His dogmatic way of talking drove his friends away.

examples.ko: 혼자 독단적으로 움직이지 말고 먼저 의논해요.
examples.en: Don't act on your own; discuss it first.

explain: 다른 사람과 의논하지 않고 혼자 판단해서 정하는 모습을 비판할 때 써요. 실제로는 '독단적인', '독단적으로', '독단적이다' 형태로 많이 말해요. 반대되는 분위기는 '민주적'이에요.
explain_en: It criticizes someone for deciding alone without consulting others. In practice it mostly appears as '독단적인', '독단적으로' or '독단적이다'. The opposite feel is '민주적' (democratic).

en: to be arrogant; to be haughty

examples.en: After he succeeded, he became arrogant.
An arrogant attitude drives people away.

examples.ko: 그는 말투가 너무 오만해서 친구가 없어요.
examples.en: His way of talking is so arrogant that he has no friends.
A player who stays humble even after winning is cool.
I do not want to look arrogant.
When you are arrogant, it is hard to admit mistakes.

explain: '오만하다'는 자기가 남보다 위에 있다고 생각하고 낮추어 보는 태도를 말해요. '거만하다', '건방지다'와 비슷한 말이에요. 말할 때는 '건방지다'를 더 쓰고, 오만하다는 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 반대로 스스로를 낮추면 '겸손하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 오만하다 is an attitude of thinking you are above others and looking down on them. It is close to 거만하다 and 건방지다. In speech people say 건방지다 more, while 오만하다 appears often in writing and news. The opposite, lowering yourself, is 겸손하다.

examples.ko: 허울 좋은 약속만 하고 지키지는 않았어요.
examples.en: He made fine-sounding promises but never kept them.

examples.ko: 그건 평화라는 허울 아래 이루어진 일이에요.
examples.en: That was done under the guise of peace.

examples.ko: 허울뿐인 사과는 아무 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: An apology that is only for show does not help at all.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 복지라는 허울을 쓰고 일을 시켜요.
examples.en: That company makes people work under the cover of 'welfare'.
The outward show may look plausible, but the inside is empty.
Do not be fooled by appearances; look at the substance.

explain: 겉만 번듯하고 속은 비어 있을 때 쓰는 나쁜 뜻의 말이에요. '허울 좋은 ~', '허울뿐이다', '~라는 허울 아래'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '겉치레'가 있어요.
explain_en: It has a negative tone for something that looks nice outside but is hollow inside. It is used in forms like '허울 좋은 ~', '허울뿐이다' and '~라는 허울 아래'. A similar word is '겉치레'.
